title: Each member who shares with trainers keeps up to a year of workouts in the shared free database, with no total budget
what: With sharing with trainers on (the default), the phone sends up to 12 months of workouts, up to about 280 KB, and the server keeps one copy per member of up to 300 KB (a heavy year is about 165 KB). The copy is rewritten after every saved workout. Nothing caps the total across all members, and nothing warns before this table eats into the 500 MB free database that every gym's desk also needs. A few thousand keen members would fill it on their own.
expected: The shared year is sized against the plan (a short summary per workout, or kept outside the main database), there is a total budget, and MettleUp is warned well before the database fills.
fix_line: Send a smaller year, set a total budget for shared workouts, and add an early warning on database size

title: Workout reports of up to 3 MB each are stored in the shared database with no total cap per gym
what: When the desk asks, the phone sends the member's whole workout history as a spreadsheet of up to 3 MB, and the server stores it inside the main database. The desk may ask the same member 5 times a day. Old reports are meant to go after 30 days, but they are only cleared when someone opens that member's reports again. Nothing caps the total per gym, and nothing warns before this fills the 500 MB free database.
expected: Reports live in file storage or are kept small, each gym has a total cap, old reports are cleared on a schedule, and MettleUp is warned before the database fills.
how_often: each time a desk asks for a report
fix_line: Keep report files out of the main database, cap the total per gym and clear old ones on a timer

title: My orders asks the server every 10 seconds even when no order is waiting or the server keeps failing
what: While the My orders page is on screen, the app asks the gym's server for the member's orders every 10 seconds. It keeps doing this when every order is already collected or cancelled, and it does not slow down when the server fails or is over its limit. A phone left on that page makes about 360 calls an hour against the shared free allowance.
expected: The page asks often only while an order is still being prepared, and it slows down after errors.
fix_line: Only ask every 10 seconds while an order is open, and wait longer after a failure
